transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2026-12-08
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Liam (Redwood AE), Priya (CSM), Noah (SE); Sara (Amberwood Head of Platform), David (Security), Olivia (PM), Aman (ML eng)

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then we'll run through the activation intake and open items. Um, we have about 45 minutes. 
[00:12] Sara: Hi, Sara here. Excited to get this moving, thanks.
[00:15] David: David, on security.
[00:17] Olivia: Olivia, product.
[00:18] Aman: Aman, ML.
[00:20] Priya: Priya from Redwood CSM.
[00:22] Noah: Noah SE, doing the infra stuff.

Summary (auto): Kickoff for Amberwood Financial onboarding to Redwood; discuss deployment choice (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), security/compliance needs (KMS, audit logs, SSO), expected token volumes and latency targets, proposer trial of Dedicated reserved cluster, and list of action items for next two weeks.

[02:05] Liam: Big picture — Amberwood, you mentioned wanting predictable latency, and strict audit/compliance. Can you walk us through your primary success criteria for the next quarter?
[02:18] Sara: Sure. Two things: 1) replace our slow in-house scoring endpoint with something under 200ms p50 for typical user flows, and 2) make sure logs and PII handling satisfy internal auditors — we need audit trails, KMS integration, and the ability to keep data within our cloud region.
[02:36] Noah: When you say 200ms p50, is that for single-turn scoring or multi-turn chat flows?
[02:40] Sara: Mainly single-turn scoring, like underwriting decisions. We're less sensitive for chat.
[02:46] Aman: To add, some of our models are long prompt contexts — like 1.5k tokens. Latency target is for those too ideally.

[04:00] Priya: Notes on deployment options: Hosted API gets you fastest time-to-value but has different guarantees on data residency and a shared tenancy model. Dedicated gives reserved capacity and predictability; Private/VPC is the full control option, but longer lead time.
[04:28] David: We're leaning Dedicated or Private. Our compliance folks prefer customer-managed key control and VPC, but the ops cost is a concern.
[04:38] Liam: Totally. From experience, teams often start Dedicated to validate throughput and cost then move to Private if compliance requires it. We can also provide KMS integration on Dedicated for some use cases — we should confirm Amberwood's KMS policy.

[05:15] Olivia: Budget/contractwise, any ballpark for Dedicated? We asked procurement.
[05:20] Liam: We'll share a tailored estimate. For planning, think of a baseline monthly committed throughput and hourly GPU unit pricing. Priya will share the Dedicated pricing deck after the call.

[06:02] Aman: A quick technical note — our current stack uses kserve-based endpoints with a custom kvcache layer. We want to avoid re-architecting too much. Can Redwood support prefix caching or compatible KV cache behavior?
[06:18] Noah: Yes, our runtime supports prefix/KV caching and we can map certain cache keys. There's some nuance around cache invalidation and tenancy — we can go over specifics in the infra deep dive.

[07:05] David: On encryption: we need to know what is encrypted at rest and in transit, and if Redwood can integrate with our KMS (Google KMS). Also audit logs — retention and fields.
[07:20] Priya: We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and some Dedicated configurations. Audit logs with token-level tracing are available in Redwood Console — retention tiers are configurable; we'll attach the security pack PDF.

[08:40] Liam: Can you share rough volume numbers? tokens/day, concurrent requests?
[08:45] Sara: We're estimating 30M tokens/month initially, with spikes up to 5 rps during end-of-day batch windows. Typical concurrency is low but we need headroom.
[08:58] Aman: Also, some downstream customers will hit the model with short prompts but very high QPS in certain internal microservices.

[09:30] Noah: For the token volumes you described, a small Dedicated cluster (2x A100 equiv) should cover baseline and let us optimize batching. We'll run a cost/latency sim with your sample prompts.

[10:02] Olivia: We need to validate accuracy differences if you recommend quantized model variants. Our risk folks are sensitive to any quality regressions.
[10:12] Priya: Redwood Optimize can run a quick evaluation — we'll do a small eval set comparing FP16 vs 8-bit quantized model and surface the tradeoffs in a short report.

[12:00] Sara: Timeline: auditors will re-review in about 6 weeks. Ideally we have something to show in 3–4 weeks for the audit queue. Is that realistic?
[12:12] Liam: Yes, if we spin up a trial Dedicated and run the perf/security checklist we can present to audit in 3–4 weeks. We'll need the sample prompts and token estimates — and David's KMS/audit requirements — to meet that timeline.

[13:45] David: Specific asks from security: SOC2 scope hint? We need to map which logs are available to map to our internal control requirements. Also SSO — SAML with Just-in-Time provisioning.
[14:02] Priya: We have SOC2 docs and an integration guide for SAML SSO; JIT provisioning is supported. I'll send the SSO guide and the SOC2 summary after the call.

[15:30] Noah: Networking note — if you go Dedicated in your cloud account, we have options: a peered VPC or a customer-controlled VPC with our agent. We should schedule an infra-only session with your network engineers.
[15:48] Aman: Yes, we'll need the peering diagram and egress rules.

[17:00] Olivia: Ops question — what monitoring will we get in Redwood Console? We want token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, and trace IDs to tie back to our logs.
[17:12] Priya: Console exposes per-route token spend, latency percentiles, top error types, and trace IDs that can be sampled and exported. We'll attach screenshots.

[18:30] Liam: Ok let's walk through the proposed pilot: 1) Redwood provisions a 2x-GPU Dedicated trial for 2 weeks, 2) Amberwood shares 500–1k sample prompts and expected peak scenarios, 3) SE runs perf/latency runs and an Optimize eval vs quantized variants, 4) Security and CSM validate audit/KMS/SSO integration.
[19:05] Sara: That sounds good. One note — our legal team may want a data processing addendum.
[19:12] Priya: We'll route the DPA template; procurement will follow up.

[20:00] (short pause, crosstalk)
[20:22] Noah: For benchmarks, please send prompts in plaintext plus a small synthetic load generator script if available. We'll try to mirror your concurrency patterns.
[20:30] Aman: We have a JMeter/locust script, will share.

[22:10] Olivia: Are there guardrails for hallucinations or output safety? We have financial regulatory constraints around statements that could be interpreted as advice.
[22:22] Priya: We offer prompt-level safety checks and output filters; we can also set up structured responses and function-calling patterns to constrain outputs. We'll add recommended prompt patterns in the runbook.

[25:00] David: A couple of gotchas from previous projects — token redaction, pii detection, and the ability to purge logs for specific requests. Is purge supported?
[25:15] Priya: Purge endpoints exist on Private; for Dedicated we have a workflow to scrub data and rotate keys. We'll document the purge SLA.

[27:00] Liam: Next steps recap: Priya sends SSO + SOC2 + onboarding runbook; Noah provisions the Dedicated trial and runs initial bench; Amberwood to provide prompts, usage numbers, JMeter script, and KMS/audit list. We aim to have trial up by 2026-12-15.

[28:30] Sara: Quick clarification — will we be billed for the trial Dedicated cluster?
[28:40] Liam: Trial runs can be offered as a time-limited credit, we'll note that in the email. Procurement will confirm.

[30:00] (questions/brief pause)
[31:10] Olivia: Any dependencies on us for network peering?
[31:18] Noah: Just firewall rules and acceptable CIDR ranges; we'll send a checklist.

[33:00] Action item readback.
[33:20] Priya: I'll send the onboarding packet and schedule the infra deep dive.
[33:25] Sara: We'll prioritize getting the prompts and scripts over.

[34:45] Liam: Anything else?
[34:50] Aman: One micro ask — can Redwood run a quick token-cost estimate for FP16 vs 8-bit given our 30M tokens/month?
[34:58] Priya: Yes, we'll include that in the Optimize report.

[36:00] Olivia: Ok good. Thanks everyone.
[36:05] David: Thanks.
[36:10] Noah: Thanks all.
[36:12] Liam: We'll follow up with the notes and links. Expect the email with attachments within 24 hours.

End of transcript. Shared artifacts referenced: onboarding runbook (link: redwood.com/docs/onboarding-runbook.pdf), Dedicated pricing deck (link: redwood.com/sales/dedicated-pricing.pdf), SOC2 summary (attached), SSO guide (link), JMeter script (customer to share).

Recording ends.
